title: Federal IT risk ratings can understate project exposure while oversight and delivery outcomes remain open
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-27-108416 review of Federal IT Dashboard investment risk ratings
geography: United States federal agencies and major information-technology investments

observations.period: Fiscal year 2025 investment sample and October 7, 2026 GAO report

denominator.unit: major IT investments assessed by GAO across 12 selected agencies

rating_alignment.value: GAO assessments matched CIO ratings 27 times, identified more risk 24 times, and identified less risk two times
rating_alignment.unit: reported comparison of 53 investment risk assessments

stale_ratings.unit: CIO ratings not updated in a timely manner according to agencies' processes

rating_process_gap.unit: agencies whose rating processes spanned longer than quarterly, contrary to OMB guidance

investment_scale.unit: more than $100 billion in annual federal IT and cyber investment spending

system_transition.value: OMB announced steps to sunset the Dashboard and replace it with a streamlined system, without providing a release timeframe

open_recommendations.unit: open GAO recommendations to nine agencies to improve risk-rating quality and frequency

delivery_conversion.unit: project completion, cost overrun, schedule delay, service reliability, public access, cybersecurity harm, or user trust

observations.method: Structured extraction from GAO-27-108416, based on fiscal-year 2025 budget data, agency rating processes, risk documentation, review of 53 selected investments, comparison of CIO ratings with GAO assessments, and recommendation-status review. Rating alignment, timeliness, process cadence, system transition, recommendations, and delivery outcomes are retained as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The 53 investments were selected from major investments at 12 agencies and are not a census of all federal IT projects. GAO's assessment of more or less risk is not itself a measure of project failure, realized cost, service quality, cybersecurity harm, or public experience. The announced Dashboard transition has no stated release timeframe in the source.
observations.subgroup: Federal agencies, oversight bodies, IT investment managers, and people who depend on public digital services supported by major federal IT investments.
observations.counterinterpretation: Differences between CIO and GAO ratings may reflect different assessment timing, documentation, or criteria rather than confirmed project failure; older ratings can coexist with lawful review cycles, while a replacement dashboard could improve oversight if it preserves timely, comparable, and inspectable risk information.

related_sources.claim: The official accessible report contains the investment sample, rating comparison, timeliness, system-transition, and recommendation findings.
The official GAO highlights summarize the rating comparison and oversight risk.

boundary: This record advances a bounded federal IT investment rating-to-oversight route. It does not establish population-wide project failure, realized cost or schedule outcomes, service reliability, cybersecurity harm, public access, user experience, or completed agency corrective action.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Canonical GAO product URL string used as a stable source identifier; accessible report and highlights links are retained for reproduction.
